passage:
Nirmala's voice note arrived while Gurpreet was counting cash from the month's tuition classes. "Two more people and my bonus doubles. Join today, the offer ends Friday. Bring your savings and two others, and we all win."

Gurpreet listened twice. The savings were meant for a laptop. Nirmala had been kind through a bad year, and saying no felt like disloyalty. But a search of the scheme's name turned up a warning on a regulator's website about schemes that pay for recruiting people.

Gurpreet called back. "I care about you, and that is why I'm saying no. I can't check where the money goes, and I won't bring anyone else into it."

Silence. "Okay," Nirmala said stiffly. "Are we still getting chai on Saturday?"

"Always."

qa.q: What were Gurpreet's savings meant for?
qa.a: The savings were meant for a laptop.

qa.q: Why did saying no feel hard to Gurpreet?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt torn, because Nirmala had been kind through a bad year, so refusing felt like disloyalty.

qa.q: What could Gurpreet do to protect both the friendship and the savings?
qa.a: Keep the savings, explain the concerns kindly, rely on the regulator's warning, refuse to recruit anyone, and keep the plan for Saturday chai.

qa.q: How might Nirmala have felt on hearing the refusal?
qa.a: Stung at first, as the stiff "Okay" suggests, but still wanting the friendship, since Nirmala asked about Saturday chai.

grounding: A friend asks Gurpreet to bring savings into a referral-bonus scheme; Gurpreet refuses kindly, checks the regulator warning and will not recruit others.

passage: "So Dhruv calls me, super excited. 'Binita, I've found this scheme. You put in your savings, you get twelve per cent a month, and if you bring two friends, you get a bonus.' Dhruv's my closest friend since school. I'm Binita, by the way. He sounded so happy. And I felt this pull, like saying no would be betraying him. But twelve per cent a month? That's not normal. So I didn't say yes that day. I searched the scheme's name on the regulator's website. It was on their warning list. That night I met Dhruv for dosa and said, gently, 'I love you, man, and I'm worried. This looks like the kind where money only comes from new people joining.' He got defensive. We didn't talk for a week. But I didn't join, and I didn't send it to anyone. When it collapsed in March, he called me first."

qa.q: Where did Binita find the scheme's name?
What was Binita feeling when Dhruv asked for the savings?
qa.a: Binita felt a pull of loyalty, as though saying no would betray a close friend, but also suspicious of the returns.

qa.q: How did Binita show loyalty without joining?
qa.a: Binita checked the regulator's warnings, told Dhruv the concerns kindly in person, refused to join, and never sent it to anyone else.

qa.q: How might Dhruv have felt when Binita raised the concern?
qa.a: Dhruv felt defensive and hurt at first, excited about the scheme, but later trusted Binita enough to call first when it collapsed.

grounding: A close friend invites the protagonist into a referral scheme; loyalty doesn't mean joining, so the protagonist checks the regulator's warnings, raises concerns kindly and recruits no one.

passage:
Sunday: Sonali, Farhan's oldest friend from college, sent him a voice note bursting with excitement: a crypto "club" that doubled your money in ninety days, plus a bonus for every member you brought in. "Join, Farhan, and add your cousins!" He felt torn. Sonali had stood by him when his father was ill.
Tuesday: Farhan looked up the club. No registration. On the regulator's website, a warning notice about schemes paying for recruitment. His stomach tightened.
Thursday: He called Sonali. "You know I'd do anything for you. That's why I'm saying this. I checked, and there's a warning about schemes like this. I'm not joining. And please don't put more in." She went quiet. "You don't trust me?" "I trust you. I don't trust them."
Two weeks later: Sonali texted: "Withdrawal button stopped working." Farhan went over with biryani, sat beside her, and helped her write the complaint.

qa.q: What did the club claim it could do with your money?
qa.a: Double it in ninety days, plus a bonus for every new member.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling after Sonali's voice note?
qa.a: He felt torn between loyalty to a friend who had stood by him and doubts about the scheme.

qa.q: How did Farhan stay loyal without joining?
qa.a: He checked the regulator's warning, told Sonali his concerns kindly, refused to join or bring in cousins, and later helped her file a complaint.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel when Farhan comes over with biryani?
qa.a: Sonali is likely embarrassed and upset about the lost money, but comforted that Farhan came without blaming her.

grounding: A close friend pushes a referral scheme; the protagonist checks the regulator's warnings, voices concerns kindly, refuses to join or recruit, and stays supportive.
